newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ business confidence malaise pandemic, says bank.
newsitem.headline: NZ business confidence malaise pandemic, says bank.

text.p: New Zealand business confidence fell further in June,according to the National Bank of New Zealand's monthly survey published on Thursday.
"Business confidence continues to slide and the malaise has become pandemic," the Lloyds TSB -owned bank said.
"No longer is the despondency restricted to the export sectors, it has filtered through to the domestic oriented sectors as well.
A net 15 percent of all respondents to the survey expect business conditions to deteriorate over the next 12 months, compared to a net 8.0 percent last month.
The agriculture sector is most despondent with a net 39 percent of respondents expecting business conditions to worsen over the coming year.
Virtually all survey indicators fell in the month, including profit, investment, construction and employment expectations.

Newly-appointed chief economist Brendan O'Donovan identified "political shenanigans", deferral of this year's tax cuts, tight monetary conditions, weak commodity prices and a standard business cycle slowdown as reasons behind the confidence slump.
He also predicted little cheer in Treasurer Winston Peters' first budget due for release at 2.00 p.m. (0200 GMT).
However, he said the Reserve Bank may provide some succour on Friday when it releases its six monthly Monetary Policy Statement.
"The Reserve Bank's forecasts are expected to show that lower interest rates can be maintained until early next year.
"The loosening of the noose may be enough to revive the business sector," he said.
Respondents were all down about the performance of their sectors with the construction sector most pessimistic.
Despite the high exchange rate, export intentions remain strong.
The bank said inflation expectations remain stuck at 2.6 percent although underlying inflation pressures were reducing.
Capacity utilisation was low and intentions in the previously buoyant construction sector had slumped.
Economy-wide pricing intentions remained low and profit expectations had slipped into negative territory.
Interest rates are expected to continue to fall in keeping with weakness in the economy.
